How horrible is the heretical people? 286.

Hanes, the last city of Egypt, near the Ethiopians and Blemmyes, 403. Through soothsayers future events are often foretold, 47. It belongs to the pagans to listen to soothsayers, haruspices, and the like, 991. Miracles of the Hebrews’ liberation, 520. Their observance, 96. What the Hebrews did not read before the age of thirty, 1095. What is the exposition of the Hebrews? 485. The Hebrews read against themselves, 1009. The riches of the Hebrew language, 488. The idiom of the Hebrew script in the syllables *im* and *oth*, 10. It is customary among the Hebrews to assign names to things from their outcome, 740. Ambiguity of Hebrew speech, 124, 136. Some criticize the Hebrew truth, 957. Hebrews believing in Christ, 13.

The Egyptians called the Heliopolitan territory a *nome*, 288. Herodotus and Berossus relate that the Assyrians perished through pestilence, 461. Who are the Etruscans? 816. Jerome’s practice in writing commentaries, 994. His adversaries slander him, ibid. He does not approve Saint Basil’s commentaries on a certain passage of Isaiah, 88. About thirty years earlier he had written a treatise on this prophet’s vision, ibid. He testifies that he had Gregory of Nazianzus as his teacher in the Holy Scriptures, ibid. He wrote on the Epistle to the Ephesians, 833. He adds other volumes published against Rufinus and Jovinian, ibid. He had written on Matthew and the book addressed to Algasia before explaining Isaiah, 506. He had written on Zechariah before explaining Isaiah, 630. He resolves the question proposed to him by Eustochium concerning the eight verses of Psalm XIII, 665. He is constrained in his understanding of certain doctrines and of the Book of Revelation, 767. Jerome must labor so that the Latin reader may understand the Hebrew etymology briefly, 840. He wishes to kill with the arrows of the Scriptures, 244. He argues against the Jews, 209. He rebukes Jewish critics, 396. He did not accept Hebrew traditions, 224. He rebukes the Seventy Translators, 707. He doubts the translation of the Septuagint, 1068. He doubts the author of the Epistle to the Hebrews, 1073. He rebukes the false interpretation of certain persons, 532. Jerome’s humility and modesty, 206, 315. He requires the testimony of a few, 493. An enemy of error, not of persons, 967. He does not condemn in martyrs what he himself refuses to follow, 975. He inveighs against the Arians, 166. He avoids slander, 841. He notes certain slanderers, 923. He lives in Palestine, 119. Jerome’s Hebrew teacher, 172, 220, 318.

Spain is called Iberia and Celtiberia, 817. The heresy of Lusitania and the Spains, 761. Sacred histories are older than profane ones, 9. It is one thing to write history and another to write prophecy, 983. Who are the writers of natural history? 960. To punish murderers is not the shedding of blood but the ministry of the laws, 987. The human being is defined as a rational animal, 37. All human beings are by nature children of God, but by their own fault they become strangers, 18. The first period of human wisdom is when we leave childhood and arrive at the rational age, 77. This age is called “morning” in the Scriptures, ibid. Among human beings the thirtieth year, and among beasts the third, is the strongest, 187. All the human beings whom histories relate are reckoned as though they were nothing, 492. Human beings pass from one purpose to another, 325. Every person seems righteous to himself, 349. Their customs are displayed in different animals, 259. They are marked as most wretched, 77. Those devoted to the world are called beasts, 404. The worthlessness of the human being is perceived through death, 177. His fragility and perpetual mutability are compared with hay, 482. Strength, even without Christ, is considered weakness, 955. How great is God’s help, and how fragile human nature is, 1066. Human perversity is inclined to excuse itself, 853. Why does God abandon a human being to his own will? 969. Those who proclaim perfect justice in a human being are condemned, 999. A delirious old woman inventing the claim that a human being can be without sin, 957. Certain wild human beings, 175. Through humility we ascend into heaven, 251. In what does humility that does not deserve praise consist? 673. The nature of the hyena, 928. Who is a hypocrite? 139.

## I

Idols are images of the dead, 462. Their manufacture, 497. From what wood they are made, 489. Their various kinds are noted, 544, 911. An apostrophe addressed to idols, 504, 505. After Christ’s coming they all fell silent, ibid. They did not foretell the future, ibid. Their responses were ambiguous, ibid. Why are they compared with moles and bats? 42. Prophetic speech is woven together concerning their mockery, 527. The ancient practice of idolatry in Egypt and elsewhere is described, 782. The Israelites imitated it, ibid.

According to the philosophers, everything we see will perish by fire, 588. The Roman emperors submit their necks to the yoke of Christ and defend his Church by their authority, 725. In what do impiety and iniquity differ? 880. Great impiety consists in not avoiding sins and not even wishing to understand them, etc., 886. Who is an impious person? 349. It is one thing to be impious and another to be a sinner, 386. The impious person is a bridle for peoples leading to ruin, 418. In the destruction of the impious, the Lord’s will and command are fulfilled, 1023. The unbelieving impious are handed over to the everlasting sword, 1022. They are compared with a sea that never rests, 684.

The entire mystery of the Incarnation is explained, 155, 1069. What is its effect? 290. Who are the uncircumcised and unclean? 601. Unbelievers will suffer different punishments according to the diversity of their merits, 33. Many spices come from India through the Red Sea, 887. Infants will rise again as perfect men, 1065. It is a great misfortune to learn songs of lamentation from women, 367.

Hell is beneath the earth, 105, 179. It is said to have a soul, although it is not an animal, 79. It is the place of punishments and torments, 250. An angel is said to preside over those there, ibid. The eternal burning of hell, 421. Just as a lake receives waters descending into it, so hell receives souls, 252. What is the innermost place? 178. “The deep” signifies hell, and “the high place” the heavens, 106.

Weakness is doubled if bodily sickness is accompanied by illness of the soul, 15. To waste away through a long illness is God’s anger, 951. Every injustice is a judgment of blood, 438. The innocent receive a reward for blood poured out on behalf of Christ, 1065. Through poverty many are converted to the Lord, 324. It is much better simply to confess ignorance than to make others heirs of one’s incompetence, 998. What do islands signify in the Scriptures? 508. Historical interpretation clings to the letter, 176. A pious interpretation not approved by Jerome, 195. A delirious interpreter is noted, 934. A Latin interpreter deceived, 779. The exposition of a certain perverse interpreter, 1017. The criticisms of the envious, 369. Who is useless to himself and to everyone? 49. The Ionian Sea, 817.

Irenaeus explained the origins of many heresies, 761. Isaac always had the same name and was content with one wife, 756. [Col. 0952] Isaiah—who was he? 211. He prophesied under four kings, 89, 90. Four prophets—Isaiah, Hosea, Joel, and Amos—prophesied at the same time, 7. Isaiah’s book contains all the mysteries of the Lord, 3. He speaks chiefly about the tribe of Judah and Benjamin, 7. In it prophecy is joined to history, 460. The prophet is wrapped in many obscurities, 326. In explaining him, the intellects of the Greeks, but not those of the Latins, labored, 5. By the number of verses he is equal to, or greater than, the Twelve Prophets, 5. There were 150 years between Isaiah and Jeremiah, 400. The Ascension of Isaiah and the Apocalypse, 761. He calls himself not a prophet but the son of a prophet, 460. He does not dare to praise the Lord, 93. What was the cause of his mourning? 335. Why he was killed by the Jews, according to the opinion of the Hebrews, 19. His death and punishment according to Jewish tradition, 666.

The Ishmaelites dwell in tents and flee through a vast wilderness, 218. Asor is their capital, ibid. Israel is interpreted as “a mind seeing God,” 13. He is found to have in Abraham the warmth of faith, 779. He is called both a nation and a people, 13. The Israelites are called firstborn, not only-begotten, 11. The people of Israel received the promised land not through their own merit but through the virtues of their fathers, 1089. The ten tribes of Israel that were in Samaria were called Ephraim and Israel, 6. What is the difference between Israel and Judah? 72. Israel is more righteous in comparison with Judah, 859. The people of the ten tribes are called the crown of pride, 372. Their glory is compared with a crown of various flowers, ibid. There was no kind of sin that was absent from the people of Israel, 14. They always limped between idols and God, 143. They desired the head of an Egyptian ox, 556. The Israelites, devoted to idolatry, had household gods, 672. Israel’s hands are bloody, 736. He was ravaged not only by the Romans but by all nations, 808. Why he lies pierced and slaughtered, 16. Italy was formerly called Hesperia, 87.

## J

Jacob and Ephraim seized the birthright, 1062. Jacob endured harsh things for one daughter, 805. In what sense are his days called “few and evil”? 982. Where many kinds of jasper are found, 638. Jaza, a city overlooking the Dead Sea, 186. The Lord left us solemn days of fasting, 689. When fasting and prayers are beneficial, 940. In what does true and false fasting consist? 687. Let our fasting not be profit for the purse, 691. It entails affliction and humiliation of the soul, 690. God accepts that which does not have leisure for good works, 21. Jephthah’s sacrifice did not please God, but his intention did, 897.

What are Jeremiah’s prerogatives? 999. Some suspect that he existed before his conception, 837. His prudence, humility, and patience, 1038. Jeremiah and Ezekiel prophesied the same things and at the same time, 1053. As simple in words as he is profound in the majesty of his meanings, ibid. He wishes the false prophet to speak the truth more than himself, 1037. Cruel priests, through envy of his holiness, against him, 1027.

Jerusalem is situated in the tribe of Benjamin, 881. It was built on rocky mountains, 570. It is called the city of the sanctuary, 601. It alone in the world received the law, ibid. Zion and Jerusalem are understood in four ways in the Scriptures, 569. It was devoted to idolatry, 668. In Jerusalem and Samaria the same idols are found as among the nations, 144. Sodom receives the name of righteousness in comparison with Jerusalem, 853. All the demons are said to have dwelt in it, 445. In what way is it a prostitute and adulteress? 673. The revolt of Jerusalem was divided into three factions, 52, 804. The Romans, Gauls, and Spaniards were called by God to besiege it, 87. It was captured forty-two years after the Lord’s Passion, 93. Jerome saw with his own eyes the destruction of Jerusalem and the Temple, 17. Its extreme desolation is described, 444. It was not struck as severely as it had struck Christ and the Apostles, 364. It is called Aelia after Aelius Hadrian, 976.

Joatham’s impieties—what were they? 101. Jod and Vav differ only in size, 143. The virginity of John the Evangelist is praised, 658. Jonah is rebuked by God: it would have been more useful to him to lie than for Nineveh to perish, 1037. One cannot sail from Joppa to India, 41. Which cities are situated on the bank of the Jordan? 129. Josephus wrote about the Jewish captivity, 766. He is refuted, 208. His error is noted, 288. Jovinian’s criticism is refuted, 951. Jubal was the inventor of the lyre, 77.

The tribe of Judah is situated in the southern part, 403. All Judaea borders on Moab, 189. Its cities are called islands, 711. They have been reduced to solitude, 916. Why? 281. Scripture speaks according to the position of the land of Judaea, 868. It is said to possess the shadow of piety, 282.

[Col. 0953] In what sense are the Jews called children of God and children of iniquity? 14. The goods of the present age were promised to them, so that, invited at least by present benefits, they might do what was commanded, 24, 723. God demanded obedience from them, 522. God rebukes them for having trusted in a human being, 224. They were always unbelieving toward the Lord’s commands, ibid. The Lord, from protector of the Jewish people, became their adversary, 754. Their solemnities were types of future things, 276. Once religion was removed, all their festivity perished, 389. Through a very evil custom they sacrificed in the mountains, 455. By sacrificing their children to idols, they make their own bellies their children’s tombs, 975. By whom the Jewish people was ruled from Jehoiakim to Christ, 996. The Jews deserved the friendship of the Lacedaemonians, Athenians, and Romans, 15. How great were their impieties? 815, 709. The hardness of the Jews is criticized in comparison with the faith of kings and princes, 889. Their blindness, 514. Their rashness—what was it? 685. Rejection and darkness, 709. The Jews and the millenarians are noted, 627. Their opinion is refuted, 158. Their empty vows, 369. They defer their vows to the future, 232. They will receive the Antichrist as the devil’s instrument, ibid. Whom they promise to themselves in place of Christ, 704. Their tradition is rejected, 318. The Antichrist lies hidden in Jewish traditions, 705. The pride of the Jews is broken, 488. They follow a simple and deadly history, 935. They possess neither knowledge of the Scriptures nor the leaves and fruits of words, 29, 368. They strive to overturn the mysteries of Christ and the Apostles, 434, 579. They interpreted an ambiguous Hebrew word in the worse sense, 43. Things that have taken place spiritually are things that the Jews insist will take place bodily, 165. The Jews as transgressors and the Apostles are distinguished by various expressions of Scripture, 524. Their interpretations, 248, 717. A Jewish fable, 361. Under the name of Idumaea the Jews understand the Romans, 218. They carried very old children in their arms and on their shoulders, 572. Jerome calls the Jews “the Circumcision,” 154. How certain people made themselves a foreskin, 601. They have bread but without strength; they have waters but without vigor, 46. No nation is more avaricious than the Jews and Romans, 36. Under the name of the Holy Spirit they sold doves in the Temple, 660. Three times a year they came to Jerusalem, 573. After Christ’s killing, all graces and gifts were taken away from the Jews, 43. Few of them were saved, 149, 614. They sent letters to all nations so that they would not accept Christ’s Passion, 199. Three times each day they curse the Christian name, 81, 565, 604, 766. They have no judges of their own but Romans, 47. They have neither prophet nor warrior in the law, ibid. They have no power to carry weapons, ibid. When the Romans conquer the Jews, the Lord is shown to have fought, 711. What is the day of the Jews’ destruction? 971. Their final devastation occurred under Vespasian, Titus, and Hadrian, 430. Their devastation will continue to the end, ibid., 21. The description of irremediable wounds expresses their eternal captivity, 16. They were destroyed because they rejected the Gospel law, 87. They are forbidden by law to enter the Holy City, 971. In comparison with their former multitude, scarcely a tenth part remains, 100. Their confusion when they recognize Christ, 350.

Judah, “beloved” and “dear,” in comparison with Israel, 72. The idolatry of Judah and Benjamin, 374. The homeland of Judas the betrayer, 373. He was drunk not with wine but with avarice, ibid. His avarice, 706.

A person is judged with the Lord not by the authority of the ruler but by comparison with virtues, 581. In what sense is the time of judgment imminent? 246. It will not be a time of repentance but of punishments, 239. He allows no one to depart unpunished, 418. On the day of judgment the earth will bring forth all blood into the midst, 359. Then every creature will feel itself to be nothing, 38. Judgment must not be anticipated, 79. A splendid and terrifying explanation of God’s judgment, 238 and following. Let no one, however holy, proceed confidently to the Judge, 1055. Judgment must be guarded at all times, 654. One must not immediately submit to the judgment of the multitude, 53. Judgments were conducted at the gates of the Temple, 1027. The earlier judges of the Hebrew people, 28.

Beasts are called *jumenta* because they help human beings, 12. In what do an oath and perjury differ? 864. “To swear” is used for “to confess,” 863. Justice embraces all virtues, 655. Its parts are to withdraw from evil and to do good, 23. Misery exists where peace is lost and justice is absent, 729. Human justice needs God’s mercy, 1068. The Lord alone knows how to approve it, 981. What is the difference between the two kinds of justice? 762, 763. “Justice” and “works” are used ironically, 676. The just person is not one who does not sin, 81. His impatience, 981. The person who perishes in his own justice is just, 762. In what sense is the just man God’s loincloth? 931. He does not fulfill all the virtues, 1055. Those who are killed and tortured by the impious are regarded as wretched by them, 433.

[Col. 0954] ## L

All labor is brief while one is reaching the desired reward, 219. Through sweat and labor we reach the abundance of fruits, 872. The Lacedaemonians are most ready for war, 61. The custom of provoking tears in Judaea, 908.

Stone. Four orders of stones inscribed with the names of the twelve tribes, 637. The Latins delighted only in the applause of eloquence, 6. Their ears were fastidious about understanding the Scriptures, ibid. The Latin language does not express the sound of *ṣade*, 155. It is scarcely produced with clenched teeth, by pressure of the tongue, ibid. The thief passes from the cross into paradise, 654. With a lion as guardian and ruler, no one dares to approach, 1024. Leprosy is understood as a scourge, 15.

The natural law was given to all, 331. The natural law was restored, 590. Why was the law given through Moses? 331. God’s law, pure and sincere, was violated by the traditions of the Pharisees, 25, 141. The law of the Lord was first translated in Alexandria, 208. The righteousness of the law is called uncleanness in comparison with evangelical purity, 762. The opinion asserting that the ceremonies of the law must be observed in the Church is rejected, 623.

Lebanon, a mountain of Phoenicia, 397, 726. Liberality and stewardship are the greatest virtue, 674. The Hebrew books are not corrupted, 97. Apocryphal books must be avoided, 761. The breadth of the Greek language, 608. Between Hebrew and Egyptian, the language of Canaan is for the most part close to Hebrew, 296. Five cities in Egypt speak the Canaanite language, 287. Why? 296. What does it mean to speak the Egyptian language? 295. Linen cloths are applied to wounds, 16. The roots of learning are bitter, but its fruits are sweet, 840.

The breastworks of camps, 344. Luke was highly skilled in the art of medicine, 97. He knew Greek letters better than Hebrew ones, ibid. His speech smells of secular eloquence, ibid. He uses Greek testimonies, ibid. Why does he alone use testimonies from the Seventy? 378. Lucius Lavinius enjoys a multitude of supporters, 491. What does it mean to sit in the council of those who play? 949. The custom of mourners, 945, 946. It is twofold, 898. The devil’s strength is in the loins, 842. We are commanded to gird them, ibid. The light of the moon—from whom does it come? 826.

## M

Madai was the ancestor of the people of the Medes, 243. Midian and Ephah are regions beyond Arabia, rich in camels, 722. The entire and principal province of those regions is called Sheba; the queen of Sheba also came from there, ibid. The Magi came from the East, either through knowledge of their art, or etc., 553. What is said about the Magi? 290. Just as the salvation of disciples benefits holy teachers, so the ruin of deceivers has ruined their patriarchs, 403. Evil things are beneficial when they serve good things, 247. Those who misuse the services of evil things are rebuked, 1083. “Evil” is used for affliction, 533, 750.

Manasseh’s cruelty, 666. What does it mean to rise in the morning? 77. The Manichaean sought another house outside the house of the God of Jacob, 32. The blasphemies of the Manichaeans, 272. Manna had the appearance of ice, 266. What do God’s and Christ’s outstretched hands signify? 772. What does it mean to have one’s hands upon one’s head? 856. Marcion’s doctrine and blasphemies, 285, 534. He introduces two gods, 105. Marcion and Valentinus are compared with hyenas, 775.

Sea. Scripture calls all gatherings of waters “seas,” 204. What does the sound of the sea signify in the Scriptures? 88. Lake Mareotis, 204. Blessed Mary is recognized among the Prophets, 117. Her privilege of virginity, 614.

Martyrs do not perish but conquer, 665. The strength of the nations is the triumph of the martyrs, 735. The Church’s victories in the martyrs, 121. The faith of believers is confirmed by the martyrs’ wounds, 298. Secure in the Church concerning the protection of their wives and children, they proceeded securely to wars, 23. The Lord will bring the martyrs’ blood into public view, etc., 358. Demons cannot endure the ashes of martyrs, 775. Whoever is overcome in martyrdom by the pain of torments is guilty of a lighter fault than one who, without being tortured, denies Christ, 311.

Who are mathematicians and astrologers? 553. Matthew composed the Gospel in Hebrew and John in Greek, 97. Both produce testimonies from Hebrew, ibid. Matthew follows the Hebrew, 128, 507. He did not take the testimony according to the Hebrew and the Septuagint, 1064. Certain things were removed from Matthew through scribal error, 507. His humility, 459.

Mazaca, the capital of Cappadocia, received the name Caesarea from Augustus, 817. The Medes were always most powerful, 374. God calls the Medes his sanctified ones and Nebuchadnezzar his servant and his dove, 170.

True medicine comes from God, 962. It must not be despised, 352. Without God’s mercy the art of healing is powerless, 475. Physicians labor in vain unless the Lord heals, ibid. Memphis and Tahpanhes, cities of Egypt, 848. A city devoted to magical arts, 205.

Falsehood imitates truth, 1006, 1039. The instability of falsehood and the stability of God’s word, 266. Some in the Church through ignorance defend falsehood as truth, 144. The habit of lying turned into a nature, 905. The blindness of the mind is not healed except by Christ’s teaching, 120. “Measure” is called by the same name in Hebrew and Latin, 134. A hireling is noted, 276. If we consider our merits, we must despair, 765. Why do many reread Milesian tales more than Plato’s books? 491.

The millenarians are noted, 210, 339, 417. They are rebuked, 450. The vain hope of the millenarians, 635. What is the error of the millenarians? 769. Church writers favoring the error of the millenarians, 767. The kite is a very rapacious bird, 444. Who are Christ’s ministers? 723. What is the final misery? 191. The consolation of miseries is to hide one’s impiety, 54. Works of mercy and charity are commended, 690, 691. With whom are mercy and election fitted together? 247.

Moab is a province of the Arabs, 184. Its capital is Ar, which is now called Areopolis, a name composed from Hebrew and Greek, ibid. Jerome testifies that its walls collapsed in a great earthquake, ibid. Moabite harvests grow in the valleys of Rephaim, 274. From Moab came forth the lamb that was sacrificed, 189. Churches of Christ exist throughout the land of Moab, 190.

What does the mill signify figuratively? 549. Moloch is the idol of the Ammonites, 673. Swarms of monks flourished in Egypt and Mesopotamia, 210. The dreams and deliriums of Montanus and insane women, 3, 6. Montanus and his disciples are intoxicated with wine and strong drink, 375.

The death of death is called “Dormition,” 249. The death of the saints is sleep, 356. In what sense is death called “Lady”? 341. The Lord does not make death but sin, 1074. The day of death is appointed for each person not by fate but by God’s will, 469. Why are even holy men terrified by death? ibid. The distinction between death and the shadow of death, 129. The region of death is the region of sinners, 179. God alone raises the dead, 353.

Moses saw the voice of God, 854. His humility, 96. Prophetic speech foretells the women who saw the risen Lord, 367, 392. The pride and luxury of women are described, 58. Changeable garments and cloaks, women’s ornaments, 62.

The world is ruled by the Spirit who, infused within it, nourishes all things, 68. The whole world needs God’s mercy, 1055. Through the regions neighboring Israel, the conversion of the whole world is proclaimed, 722. The world is to be burned up by God’s judgment, 1091. What will it suffer at the end? 329 and following. According to ecclesiastical traditions, the world will be completed after six days, 326. At the consummation of the world, the memory of former pleasures will be the material of torments, 331.

Those who love gifts are noted, 26. Some think they can redeem God with donations and gifts, without observing the commandments, 21. Those who accept gifts from plunderers are partners of thieves, 26. Tamarisk grows in the wilderness and in salty soil, 193. According to some, hatreds arise through magical arts from the tamarisk tree, 279.

## N

Nebo and Medeba, distinguished cities, 185. The idol Nebo is said to have fallen silent after the truth of the Gospel, 544. Naboth’s piety, 300. Nebuchadnezzar, the Lord’s dove, 1024. Why is he called holy? 988, 1215. His sanctification is one thing, and that of the priests who minister to the Lord another, ibid. Nathanael sought Christ by the authority of the Scriptures, 795.

[Col. 0956] All the nations of the world are declared to believe in Christ, 610. We are good by nature and evil by will, 554. They are not different natures, as the heretics wish, 13, 670. Those who admit a double nature are questioned, ibid. The good of nature is not sufficient for righteousness, 23. Everyone desires that in which he was born, 457. What dangers overwhelm sailors? 533.

The Nazarenes did not drink wine or strong drink, 83. What was the opinion of the Nazarenes? 130, 425. What is necromancy? 389. Nemrim is above the Dead Sea, 187. Its waters are very bad and bitter, and no grass grows there, ibid. What is *neser*? 255. Nesrach, the god of the Ninevites, 466. The utterly unclean heresy of the Nicolaitans, 377.

The Nile flows from Ethiopia into Egypt, 198. It is divided and cut into seven channels, 165. Its waters are muddy, 321. Nineveh, the capital of the Assyrians, 169. Our nitre and the fuller’s herb are repentance, 850. No, a city of Egypt, now called Alexandria, 198. Interpretations of different names, 9. How the Lord is an eternal name and sign to penitents, 604. To know is one thing, to express is another, 619. The new moons of the Greeks, 826. “Night” is taken for tribulation, 348. According to the philosophers, clouds are raised no more than ten stades above the earth, 578.

## O

What constitutes the sign of obedience and the mark of contempt? 853. What is seen with the eyes is retained more firmly in the mind, 969, 973. A great offense is refusing to appease the one whom you have offended, 856. The names of those making offerings were recited publicly, 921. The power of oil, 502. What is “son of oil”? 69. In what do “burden” and “vision” differ? 184, 1067. Oolibah is interpreted as “my tabernacle is in her,” 25.

The works of God’s people do not grow old but are renewed daily, 794. In the work there is a reward, not in the promise, 1089. No work worthy of God’s justice will be found, 238. The holy person does not glory in knowledge of the Scriptures but in works, 685.

Continuous prayer ought to be in our mouth, 741. Perseverance in prayer is commended, 920. The Prophet’s persistent prayer is noted, 738. In prayer, certain impious people join days and nights together but are not heard by God, 22. One should pray secretly and in the closed chamber of the heart, 689. No one is worthy to pray for sinners, 944. It is foolish to pray for sinners unto death, 940. Profane and Christian orators are praised for the flow of their eloquence, 329. An excellent saying of the most eloquent orator, 665.

There are four regions of the world, 568. The devastation of the world in Jerome’s time, 810. The ordination of clergy is fulfilled not only by the utterance of a prayer but by the laying on of hands, 696. It should be given to saints and to those most learned in the law, and not to others, etc., ibid. Just as in the ordination of evil persons the one who appoints such people shares in their sins, so in the ordination of saints the one who chooses good people shares in their righteousness, ibid.

Origen, the allegorical interpreter, 1031, 1034, 1039, 1046. He makes the Church’s mysteries conform to his own intellect, 167. His volumes, Homilies and Excerpts, 6. Many volumes on Isaiah, ibid. Two books addressed to Grata were thought to be spurious, ibid. What are Origen’s and Eusebius Pamphilus’s interpretations of the Scriptures? 167. What is Origen’s exposition? 994. He is noted, 981. Orion has twenty-two stars, 240. The oryx is a kind of beast born in the wilderness, 597. The Jews are compared with it, ibid. According to Jerome’s opinion, Hosea does not appear to have had a prostitute as his wife, 125. What are “fattened bones”? 697. Uzziah himself is Azariah, under two names, 7.

## P
## P

The Hebrew language does not have the letter *P*, but uses the Greek *Phi* in its place, 35. Covenant and Testament are the same, 1074. Bread and water are taken in Scripture for every kind of food and drink, 45. Nothing is more grievous than the pain of women in labor, 889. Little children are instructed in the morning hours, 579. Passover (*Pascha*) signifies “passing over,” 424. The Lord came to Jerusalem for three Passovers, 390. [Col. 0957] The passions are called disturbances, 83. Those who preside ought to be free from them, ibid. A fine description of negligent shepherds, 661. The same are censured, 996 and following. Because of bad shepherds the Lord’s inheritance is trampled, 928. By our patience the name of God is glorified, 803. To love one’s homeland is natural, 891. Paula and Pammachius passed through the eye of the needle, 724. Both are praised by Jerome, ibid. From where did the apostle Paul receive his name? 278. The preaching of the Gospel was multiplied through the apostle Paul, 130. His preachings, 355. He follows the Hebrew truth, 608, 760. He uses testimonies of poets, 580. Where the authority of the apostle Paul precedes, other interpretation ceases, 149. His exposition must be followed, 567. He praises and rebukes the Corinthians according to the diversity of their inhabitants, 756. In what respect are Paul of Samosata and Photinus accursed? 958.

The Jews do not praise poverty, 50. The acceptance of the poor and the rich is condemned, 57. One must lend at interest to Christ through the poor, 946. It is dangerous to demand repayment from a poor person who is unable to pay, 687. There is no peace for the wicked, 683.

Sin is most foul-smelling, 256. It is a wall dividing God and human beings, 703. Through excessive familiarity it is changed into nature, 936. Each person is sold into slavery by his own sins, 575. The order of judgment is arranged according to the diversity of sin, 248. As many kinds of sin as we have, so many sentences of judgment do we deserve, 308. God cannot be harmed by our sins, 894. All our sins are exposed to God’s eyes, 777. Nothing so offends God as an uplifted neck after sins have been committed, 223. Those who do not wish to acknowledge their sins provoke God’s anger all the more, 856. Whoever dies in sin is lost to God and does not endure, 774. Our sins are not loosed unless we receive them from the hand of the Lord, 480. Every creature grieves over human sins, 847. Sins are various, 262. By what remedies are lesser and greater sins cleansed? 850. Lesser sins are washed away; greater ones are burned out, 66. As long as they are minor, God acts patiently, etc., 235. To have sins loosed is not the same as to have them forgiven, 480. However serious the sin, if someone turns back, he can be healed, 99. Those who wish to turn back are preserved not by their own merit but by God’s mercy, 711. The remission of sins is the cause of consolation, 479. The beginning of salvation is to understand and mourn one’s sins, 266, 863. All their remedies were sought from the Temple, 988. Excuses for sins are words of murmuring, 695. One must not sin either in speech or in deed, 700. It is difficult to find someone who is not weighed down by the bonds of sin, 694. Each person kindles a fire for himself in proportion to his sin, 584. The more frequent the admonition, the greater the sins of those who despise it, 1014. The later the punishment of sinners, the more just it is, 1088. To punish sinners is foreign and alien to God, 383. The ease of sinning and the difficulty of escaping from sins, 81. It is a lesser evil to sin openly than to pretend and feign holiness, 277. In what does their hope of salvation consist? 327. They refer their faults back to God, 757. They are punished so that sin, left unavenged, may not harm others by its example, 973. Torments are applied to them so that they may be cleansed by divine fire, 148. Their killing signifies consummated anger, 946. The divine word exhorts sinners to repentance, 409. Through stages of repentance Moabites become Israelites, 271. They die in the middle of their days, 471. It is harmful to live with sinners, 93. The Pelagians are censured, 916, 1014.

The partridge: its nature, 961. Perfection is not found on the way, 845. Who are the perfect and the beginners in the Church? 737. We are always situated in danger, 845. Some take “to perish” and “to grow old” to mean abolition, 588. Persecution pertains not to the denial of believers but to their testing and their crown, 208. In a time of persecution no one is to be trusted, 905. In a time of persecution, in whom should one place confidence? 855. The saints were killed by hunger during persecution, 785. We are cleansed through persecutions and hardships, 905. The persecutions of the Church, from Nero to Maximinus, 955. Persecutors are not to be feared, 593. Their fury and cruelty, 283. Their pride is scattered, 593. All their disgrace will pass away, 590. How the Lord delivers his own from persecutors, 838.

The Persians and Chaldaeans delight in cavalry, 926. The Persians are situated in the east, 568. Before Cyrus they were obscure, 215. They founded the cities of Seleucia and Ctesiphon in place of Babylon, 174. Perversity can never overcome what is right, 121. Among the Egyptians, Pharaoh is the name of royal power, 402. His royal house was in Tanis, ibid. Jerome discussed, after the apostle Paul, the hardening of Pharaoh, 757. Pharaoh and Herod are persecutors of male children, 805. Some think that Philip was carried off by an angel, 754, 755. The Philistines are called foreigners, 182. The Septuagint always interpreted *Philistîm* as “foreigners,” 35. Philosophers and orators applaud themselves, 438. The wisdom of philosophers and the prophecies of diviners were destroyed at Christ’s coming, 530. The most illustrious philosophers openly kept concubines, 35. Pul, king of the Assyrians, began to devastate the ten tribes of Israel under Uzziah, king of Judah, 6. What regions does the land of Phut contain? 816.

Piety and true religion are the royal road, 674. Cakes, or little pastries, are called *chavonae*, 671. Punishment or reward does not arise from God’s prejudice but from the merits of individuals, 24. From where do the eternal punishments of sinners arise? 250. Punishment unites people in the underworld, ibid. Human frailty cannot pass judgment on punishments and their measure, 337. The order and usefulness of punishments, and the fruit of repentance, 758. Fear of punishments is praised, 941. The whole punishment is not to behold God reigning in his majesty, 349. The longer God’s forgetfulness lasts, the greater the punishment of sin, 855. The magnitude of punishment is shown by bronze and iron, 577. One kind of punishment belongs to the author of an offense, another to the person compelled by its author, 255. The years of punishment of the ten tribes, Judah, and Moab are reckoned, 276.

The Carthaginians (*Poeni*) are called, through a corrupted pronunciation, almost *Phoeni*, 1018. Repentance is praised in opposition to Novatian, 327. It wounds, 538. Without God’s help we cannot perform repentance, 1066. God receives the penitent, provided that they return with weeping, 217, 863. Victory is granted to the penitent by the Lord’s grace, 592. In what does their joy consist? ibid.

The stories of the poets boast that Vibbius was raised by Asclepius, 352. Their stories and license are on the wings of the winds, 92. Porphyry’s blasphemy, 623. His slander, 55. Jerome refutes Porphyry, 402. The gates of death are sins, 344. What is an impudent petition? 853. All power, in relation to God’s anger, is compared with ash and cinder, 246. Present power is the material of future torments, 432. God’s command in a promise cannot stand according to the letter, 701. Negligent prelates should be afraid, 942. The prayers of the saints can withstand God’s anger, 894. In Scripture the firstborn do not receive the inheritance, but the second-born, 11.

The two princes of the apostles are Peter and Paul, 789. Their dispute was a matter of dispensation, 541. The betrayers of David and of Christ perished by hanging, 81. In the Lord’s promises, anger and fury must not be inserted, 712.

The certainty of prophecy, 84. Its style, 189. A question arises concerning the truth of a prophecy, 995. Prophets were first called “seers,” 7. There is one Spirit in the prophets, 406. God spoke in their minds, 4. They speak by the Lord’s will, 1039. They understood what they were saying and did not speak in ecstasy, 3. From where did they obtain faith in their own words? 165. They preceded as a sign of future events, 125. All sang of Christ’s coming, 940. They performed many things as a type of Christ, 924. What was the prophets’ manner of life? 211. A prophet is revealed by the fulfillment of his prophecy, 1038. What is prophetic custom? 57, 73, 83. Prophetic steadfastness and prudence, 1030. From where does obscurity arise? 213. In the prophets everything is full of riddles, 769. Change of persons in the prophets is difficult to understand, 902, 1070. The order of times is not preserved in them, 983, 1013. Why is it so often said in the prophets, “Thus says the Lord”? 1004. A true prophet can resist the Lord with prayers, 945. They must be asked about the ancient paths, 947. Their works are examples of virtue for us, 1080. Their promises do not pertain only to the Jews, 714. A question drawn from the prophets Isaiah and Jeremiah is resolved, 596. The prophet trembles at the sight of God, 999. He speaks in the person of those who are troubled by God’s judgments, 751. From Malachi to John the Baptist the Jewish people had no prophet, 571. Among the Jews priestly ranks had been established to distinguish prophets from false prophets, 50. False prophets are called prophets, 1035. The prophets of Samaria prophesied in the idol Baal, 1000. The prophets of the nations pretend that they proclaim future events by the divine Spirit, 1034. The kinds of prophesying and revelations, 1004. In prosperity we must always beware of what is to come, 553.

A most beautiful exposition of the sayings of Proverbs, 629. Some deny God’s providence to irrational creatures, 1090. Nothing is more foolish than not to foresee the last things, 961. [Col. 0959] Who is prudent in mystical speech? 50.

In the Psalms there is lyric poetry, 1013. The title in four psalms, 589. The ninth Psalm is against the devil, 234. Psalms VIII and LXXXIII are inscribed “For the winepresses,” 748. Psalm Forty-Four pertains to the mystery of Christ and the Church, 327.

Tax collectors and prostitutes became trees of excellent fragrance, 653. Chastity is not in bodily weakness but in the will of the mind, 659. Forgiveness is granted to that childhood which is adorned with modesty, 838. The Punic language flows from the sources of Hebrew, 110. It is related to Hebrew, 1018. The punishment of purgatory is established, 830. Pyrrhus, king of the Epirotes, 504.

Rabshakeh imitates the custom of the prophets, 454.

Reason. What seems to us not to have reason is full of justice and reason, 910.

Various regions are noted, 1018, 1019. Many regions are now called Arabia, 217. The whole region around Lydda, Joppa, etc., is suitable for feeding flocks, 780. What does it mean to keep the Sabbath? 655. In what does its observance consist? 699, 900, 783. It cannot be fulfilled according to the letter, 699. God does not seek sacrifices but the disposition of those offering them, 784. Believers cannot offer sacrifices carnally, ibid. What is appropriate to those who offer sacrifices from plunder? 888.

The brevity of worldly happiness, 473. Whoever trusts in worldly things forgets God, 936. The world is called the sea, 316. Saturn’s Golden Age, 159, 416. [Col. 0960] Solomon assumed the kingdom in the twelfth year of his age, 51. We ought not to be content with our own salvation, 309. The more merciful is the one who shows the way of salvation after sin, the more wretched is the one who, etc., 858.

Why are many not saved? 753. Samaria was called Sebaste, 203. Where did the kingdom of Samaria and Syria come to an end? ibid.

Every saint is a throne of God, 943. The saints are not inhabitants of the earth, 841. They need God’s mercy, 578. They complete their days, 471. They have the wings of an eagle and a dove, 253. They ask that God not spare them in this world, 962. God gives power to the wicked so that the faith of the saints may be displayed, 977. God shows that he is held back by their prayers, 1036. Health is more welcome after sickness has been driven away, 1053. The book of Wisdom is inscribed with Solomon’s name, 753. What wisdom is to be pursued? 645. A wise person who thinks that anything can be done without God’s wisdom and protection is wise in vain, 396. Secular wisdom was overturned by the preaching of the cross, 613. It is foolish, and its teachers are foolish, 293. Wisdom is taken for wickedness, 1042. The Stoics’ distinction between wisdom and prudence, 83.

Sarah’s name signifies “princess,” 570. Sargon, king of the Assyrians, was called by seven names, 211. What are Sharon and Bashan? 436. Saul was deceived by desire for plunder, 353. The scribes and Pharisees, together with Herod, slaughtered many thousands of little children, 112. They are called mockers and pestilent persons, 785.

All the Scriptures are inspired by the Holy Spirit, 393. They are called one book, ibid. Christ is the foundation of the meaning of Scripture, 3. The divine majesty of Scripture is to be admired, 728. It is wrapped in the mysteries of future things, 284. The authority of Scripture must be followed, 126. Ignorance of Scripture is ignorance of Christ, 1. Knowledge of Scripture among the nations, 512. Jerome exhorts people to understand Scripture, 284. Blessed is the one who sows in the words of Scripture, 13. One learned in the holy Scriptures is a bulwark of the Church, 638. The teaching of Scripture is pure silver, 25. In the exposition of Scripture, truth is to be sought, not contention, 44.

The meaning of Scripture has been weakened through allegory. After the truth of the history, everything in Scripture is to be understood spiritually, 3. In Scripture the letter must be trampled down, and the fruit of the life-giving Spirit must be gathered, 13. The simple words of Scripture are straw; its inner meaning is wheat, 157. One must not flatter princes in such a way that the truth of the holy Scriptures is neglected, 451. The error of parents and ancestors must not be followed, but the authority of Scripture and the command of God who teaches, 907. Scripture wishes the people to be taught not only through the ears but also through the eyes, 973. Those who receive Scripture otherwise than the Holy Spirit expresses it are called false prophets, 1043. Those who do violence to Scripture are rebuked, 1022. Scriptures give Jews and heretics an occasion of error, 313. Who is the false teacher and corrupter of Scripture? 25. It is the custom of Scripture to provoke people to repentance, 271. Many things in Scripture are said according to the opinion of the time in which the events are reported to have occurred, 1038. What do the apostles observe when reciting testimonies from Scripture? 622, 665. The apostles took the testimonies of Scripture according to the Hebrew text, 378, 394. The particularity of holy Scripture is praised, 509. What is the custom of Scripture? 201. The idiom of holy Scripture, 171, 191, 205.

Many ecclesiastical writers are censured, 451. In what sense does Jerome call them teachers of the Church? ibid. Certain things were altered by inexperienced writers, 644. An addition by bad writers, 642. The fault of scribes is displayed, 995.

Security and despair are to be avoided, 1042. Security produces negligence, and negligence contempt, 354, 1089. *Sedec* is a Hebrew word and signifies “just” more precisely than “justice,” 25. Segor, the fifth city after Sodom, etc., was preserved through Lot’s prayers, 187. The Hebrews think that Shem was Melchizedek, 497.

Through the senses the strength of the soul grows soft, 334. Through all the senses death enters for the destruction of the soul, 908. Those who indulge their senses are condemned, 332. Through all the senses one arrives at understanding, 968. We ought to understand what is right by natural sense, 879. Human beings abuse the gift of sense and speech, which was given so that they might perceive and hear God, 41. To argue about God’s words according to human sense is sacrilege, 1069.

Among the Hebrews, “seven” is understood as “many,” 626. [Col. 0961] The number seven is holy, 1083. The numbers seven and seventy signify perfect repentance, 327. Why are the numbers seven and ten familiar to the Jews? 64.

The Septuagint edition is commonly used throughout the world, 792. They translate the name *Sabaoth* in two ways: either “Lord of hosts” or “Lord almighty,” 18. They refused to translate into Greek a clear prophecy about Christ, 43. They did not dare to interpret openly that the child was to be called God, 133. They change the meaning of prophecy, 565, 945. In very many places they disagree with the Hebrew truth, 269. They inserted not the words of Scripture but their own meaning, 341. An addition by the Septuagint: “pierced with a spit,” 120. They added from their own material, 143. They omit certain things, 956. The cause of an omission in the Septuagint, 1056. A verse was not in the Septuagint, 1017. The error of the Septuagint translators, 461. Jerome defends the Septuagint translators, 415. Jerome is compelled to interpret the Septuagint edition, 420. In their interpretation the Septuagint imitates the stories of the nations, 245. The Septuagint and Theodotion name many things in imitation of the stories of the nations, 236. What the Septuagint edition lacked in the Latin and Greek texts, 1008. Many things are missing in the Greek and Latin manuscripts of the Septuagint, 1035. Additions made by Origen in the Greek copies, taken from Aquila’s edition, 42. The Alexandrian manuscripts contain things that are not in the Hebrew or Septuagint copies, 696. What was added in the Church’s copies from the Hebrew and from Theodotion, 100.

The Seraphim are angelic powers, 93. Those who understand the two Seraphim as the Son and the Holy Spirit are rebuked, 92. Others wish them to signify the Old and New Testament, 93.

The divine word, conceived in the mind, burns in the breast, 980. Why is the divine word divided into parts? 560. It uses the words of ordinary human usage, 487. Whoever is free from marital servitude is truly a servant of Christ, 657. What are the inheritance and rewards of God’s servants? 642. Shallum is Sedecias himself, 989. What are Setta and Settim? 502. What is *sicera*? 76, 374.

Signs. Many who received signs, 106. What is the sign of great sterility? 938. The fountain of Siloam is at the foot of Mount Zion, 119. The scarcity of its waters, 937. Simon and Elymas were magicians who resisted the apostles Peter and Paul, 641. Mount Sinai is situated in the southern region, 568. “Bosom” is explained in two ways, 777. Sometimes it is called “head,” ibid.

Zion and Jerusalem are one city, 506. Zion, the mountain on which Jerusalem was built, was called the city of David, 24. Why is Zion called a virgin and daughter? 463, 464, 744. Why is it called a valley and not a mountain? 220. It is no other thing than the people of God, 594. No one dwells in Zion except one who is holy, 410.

The nature of sirens, 521. Through a deadly crime they plunge souls into the deep, 246. What does Jerome understand by them? 175. Socrates is falsely praised, 508. The sun is called by three names, 336. The course of the sun, moon, and other heavenly bodies is defined, 492. The sun and moon will receive the rewards of their course, 415. In what does consolation amid evils consist? 337.

Dreams. Why did the wicked see dreams? 1004. Dreamers in the Church proclaiming their errors, ibid. *Sorec* is a kind of excellent vine, 69, 850. Hope in God is commended, 583. By hope of future things we endure tribulation, 680. The defenses of those who do not hope in God are quickly scattered, 873.

The Holy Spirit is of the same nature as the Father and his Son, 753. His riches, 681. Among the Hebrews it is referred to in the feminine gender, 485. The Spirit is incorporeal, 754. It watches toward God, and in what manner, 348. That stars exist in the sky by day is proved by an eclipse of the sun, 240. God called the stars by their names, ibid. The Stoics agree with us in their definition of good and evil, 159. The nature of ostriches, 245.

What is the voice of pride? 177. Pride must be avoided with every effort, 224. Ruin follows pride, and glory follows humility, 241. Many fall into pride through their reputation for virtue, 877. Pride is taken for power and glory, 735. Every proud person is ready to commit an injury, 241. The superstition of the wicked concerning knowledge of the future, 775. Why was Susanna’s history not accepted by the Hebrews? 1048. Sycamore wood is cheap, cedars are imperishable, 136. What is sycophancy? 883. Hebrew has extended syllables, 733. The syllogism in Scripture, 1077. Symmachus, according to his custom, translates Scripture more clearly, 7.

Tabeel is either a man or an idol, 203. The end of the tabernacles is possession of the eternal house, 628. The mole is an animal without eyes and harmful to crops, 42. Tanis was the metropolis of Egypt, 205. Tiglath-pileser, king of the Assyrians, while Pekah was reigning in Samaria, transferred the Israelites into Assyria in the fifty-second year of the reign of Uzziah, king of Judah, 7.

The Temple was situated on the threshing floor of Ornan, 216. Angels are guardians of the Temple, 605. A voice is said to have come forth from its inner shrine, etc., ibid. When the Lord turns his face away from us in temptations, we are dashed to pieces, 764. The terebinth market is accursed to the Jews, 1065. Tertullian, 478.

The foundations of the earth are the will and power of God, by which all things are contained, 242. They are carried by angelic powers, 529. The earth is called a point and human beings locusts, 474. What does it mean to work one’s land? 324. What is the land of the living? 701. “Earth” is taken for the soul, 359. Nothing is fatter than the promised land, 68. Its boundaries, ibid. No region is found equal to the promised land, 457. How great was the terror of the inhabitants of the promised land at the arrival of the people of God? 194.

The two Testaments are joined by unity, 95. The New Testament is strengthened by testimonies of the Old, 316. Nothing succeeds the New Testament, 795. We were once strangers to God’s Testament, having no hope and being without God, 720. In Hebrew, *Tharsis* is called “sea,” 816. Thecua, a village separated from Jerusalem by twelve miles, 881. Frankincense comes from Sheba, 887.

From where does fear of human beings arise? 593. It is more grievous to see the one whom we fear than to endure the torment of punishments, 1081. What fear preserves the souls of the saints whole and pure? 582. God protects those who fear him in religion, ibid. Titus and Vespasian offered the spoils from the Temple to the Capitol, 390.

The winepress in Scripture is used for vengeance and for the gathering of fruits, 748. It signifies the Lord’s Passion, 155. The torments of some are remedies for others, 858. Many use a false translation, 93. Tribulations correct, 354. Present tribulation is compensated by future joy, 642, 979.

The mystery of the Trinity in one divinity, 92, 397. Unity of substance and fellowship of majesty in the divine persons, 90. When the Father says, “I will not give my glory to another,” he does not exclude the Son, 509. The correct confession of the Holy Trinity is ignorance of knowledge, 767. At the Lord’s command, the Trinity commands, 95. The Holy Trinity dwells in the Church, 356, 766. Confession of the Trinity is the holy mountain and doctrine of truth, 659. While sin reigns in us, we cannot know the mysteries of the Holy Trinity, 89.

Tully interpreted the *Timaeus*, which discusses the harmony of the world, 491. The obscurity of this author is noted, ibid. Many things that are disgraceful in reality are expressed in respectable words, 550.

What are the ornaments of cities? 58.

## V

In Scripture “wind” is understood in three ways, 763. All pomp of words will be reduced to nothing, 75. Among the Hebrews “word” is used for “thing,” 475, 1090. There is a great contest over a single word, 869.

Truth must always be loved, and the multitude of human beings must not be feared, 842. Truth can be shut up and bound, but it cannot be conquered, 1009. The light of knowledge and truth drives away all errors, 693. There is one way of truth and many of falsehoods, 674. There is beauty in truth and disgrace in falsehood, 912. After error has been perfected, we receive truth more easily, 718. Truth and steadfastness must not be abandoned in hardships, 1028. In the Old Law there is the shadow of truth, 736. The snares of truth, 540. Each adversary believes that truth is with him, 105.

The word “evening” and the west receive different interpretations in Scripture, 308. Whoever has the beginning of sins is in the evening, ibid. The bat is a nocturnal bird, sounding not so much with voice and song as with a screech, 42.

What is the royal road? 676. The difference between victims and sacrifices, 660. Why were victims granted to the Jewish people? 718. Human victory is not perfect, 200. There is no certain victory in this world, 1079. Victorinus the martyr was unskilled in speech, not in knowledge, 3. He wrote on Isaiah, ibid. The widow who is supported by the Church’s provisions, 51. The mystery of the two rods is explained, 630. False virginity is condemned, 892. What does the word of God accomplish in a virginal soul? 118.

“Visitation” signifies consolation and punishment, 1081. “Visitation” is taken not for a remedy but for a blow, 188. Vices have the images of beasts, 576. According to the diversity of vices, among the proud some are mountains and others hills, 40. Vices and sins are unripe grapes, 1074. Peace follows the cleansing of vices, 867. Vices do not follow one another, but virtues do, in which all things are balanced, 611. It is our vice that we are overwhelmed by the fruits of the sea, 302.

All the virtues follow one another and adhere to one another, 275, 655. Unless vices withdraw, virtues do not enter, 412. [Col. 0964] The gates of righteousness are works of virtue, 344. Under the heading of righteousness all the virtues are understood, 636. We cannot immediately grasp perfect virtue as soon as we wish, 275. Vain glory in virtues must be avoided, 936. The people of God is understood through virtues, 736. According to the variety of virtues there are differences of dwellings, 256. The Temple of the Lord is that in which the choir of all the virtues dwells, etc., 891. Whoever imitates a particular virtue is called its son, 702. “Virtues” is used for miracles, 750.

A quiet death is preferable to a miserable life, 982. Eternal life is the promise of all good things, 646. In the Old Testament it is said that the people saw the voice of God, 8. We are evil by will, not by nature, 258. It lies within our power either to do something or not to do it, 890. By our own will we do not receive the word of God, 884. By his own will each person is trampled down by vices, 699. Those whom the love of pleasure and riches surrounds are rebuked, 322. The one who is holy in body and spirit offers and fulfills a vow to the Lord, 298. What is the vow of a righteous man? 629. The unlearned crowd easily changes its opinion, 1028.

## X

Xenophon wrote a history of Cyrus, 522.

## Z

*Zythum* is a kind of drink made from grain and water, 292. In Dalmatia it is called *sabajum*, ibid.

## TRANSLATION OF NINE HOMILIES OF ORIGEN ON THE VISIONS OF ISAIAH

**Homily One.** On this passage of Isaiah: “And it came to pass in the year in which King Uzziah died: I saw the Lord sitting upon a lofty throne,” 901.

**Homily II.** On what is written: “Behold, a virgin shall conceive in the womb,” etc., 906.

**Homily III.** On the seven women, 909.

**Homily IV.** On the vision of God and the Seraphim, 912.

**Homily V.** On what is written: “Who raised up righteousness from the East?” and again on the vision, 916.

**Homily VI.** On what is written: “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” through the passage where he says, “And they will be converted, and I will heal them,” 920.

**Homily VII.** On what is written: “Behold, I and the children,” etc., 928.

**Homily VIII.** On what is written: “Howl, carved images, in Jerusalem and in Samaria,” through the passage where he says, “And I will shake the cities that are inhabited,” 932.

**Homily IX.** On what is written: “And I heard the voice of the Lord saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go to this people?” and, passing over a little, through the passage where it is written: “Ask for yourself a sign from the Lord your God, either in the depth or in the height,” 934.
